clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the Humanitarian Service Medal with accompanying ribbons and appurtenances for award by the Secretary of Defense or, with regard to the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation, and defines eligible persons (members of the Armed Forces, including Reserve Components, who after April 1, 1975 distinguished themselves by meritorious participation in a military act or operation of a humanitarian nature). Executive Order 13286 section 55, effective March 1, 2003, struck the Secretary of Transportation wherever it appears in sections 1, 2 and 4 and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security (before: the Secretary of Transportation, twice in section 1; after: the Secretary of Homeland Security). The section continues as amended, has no end date, and is printed in the current U.S. Code note as amended. Operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11965 of January 19, 1977 (42 FR 4329; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11965.txt, read in full) has four sections: section 1 establishes the Humanitarian Service Medal with ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of Defense or, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation, and sets eligibility (members of the Armed Forces who after April 1, 1975 distinguished themselves by meritorious participation in a military act or operation of a humanitarian nature); section 2 provides for the design, uniform regulations and order of precedence; section 3 limits the medal to one per person with devices for later participation; section 4 allows posthumous award. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The only later instrument found is Executive Order 13286 section 55 (68 FR 10619, 10629; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), which struck the Secretary of Transportation wherever it appears in sections 1, 2 and 4 and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security; it is recorded as a later event on sections 1, 2 and 4 and does not touch section 3. A search of the held Federal Register texts of orders numbered above 11965 for citations of this order found only Executive Order 13286. The Office of the Federal Register note records only the Executive Order 13286 amendment. The U.S. Code prints the order as amended under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09). The three bounded searches show no revocation. All four sections are operative on 2026-10-14. Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.
